scope: Local generated-fixture validation of native selective NAS-copy source code. No live NAS, Storage Box, Arr, or Plex operations were performed by these checks.

linux_unit_tests.command_summary: Run python3 -m unittest discover -s /work/tests -p test_native_library.py -q in the existing local Podman image with repository scripts/tests mounted read-only.
linux_unit_tests.atomic_publication: Exercised the real Linux libc renameat2 RENAME_NOREPLACE implementation, including refusal to overwrite an existing empty destination.

real_rclone_smoke.command_summary: Run generated local fixture driver with the actual rclone 1.75.1 binary and an alias remote backed by an ephemeral local directory; use no network and no credentials.
behaviors_verified: Real rclone lsjson discovers exactly the selected generated movie and TV titles.
Real rclone hashsum sha256 and copy feed independent local verification.
Movie and TV copies publish through Linux exclusive rename into their respective final roots.
Repeating both pulls succeeds after verifying the existing local copies.
Snapshot reports two verified local titles.
Explicit local eviction removes each owned final title.
Canonical fixture files remain present and their SHA-256 values remain unchanged after all operations.
real_rclone_smoke.tv_copy_gate: Enabled only in this isolated fixture environment.

acceptance_limits: Synthetic bytes are not playable media; this is source/runtime validation only.
The rclone remote was local, so this does not establish live SFTP server-side checksum support or NAS network throughput.
No native title was copied to the real NAS by this validation.
No Plex library root was changed, title indexed, or device playback tested.
Real NAS/Plex acceptance and TV-library migration remain separate unfinished work.
